metadata.technology: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe (with MCU + radio)
metadata.technology_specification: Capacitive soil moisture sensor probe with integrated microcontroller unit (MCU) and wireless radio module
metadata.technology_reasoning: Capacitive soil moisture sensors are widely used for soil moisture measurement due to their resistance to corrosion and stable readings over time. The integration of a microcontroller and radio module (often low-power wireless like LoRa, Zigbee, or BLE) is common in modern IoT-enabled soil moisture probes for remote sensing and data transmission.

components.reasoning: Core sensing element responsible for detecting soil moisture via capacitance changes; universally present and a distinct separate component.
Controls sensor operation, data processing, and communication; always a distinct electronic component in integrated sensor systems.
Enables remote data transmission; usually procured or integrated as a separate module utilizing standard protocols (e.g., LoRa, Zigbee, BLE).

components.component: Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy Harvesting Unit)
components.reasoning: Necessary for autonomous operation; typically a distinct component such as a rechargeable battery or energy harvester.
Physical substrate integrating the MCU, radio, power management, and sensor interface; a standardized manufacturing component.
Protects electronic components and sensor elements from environmental damage while allowing soil contact; usually a separate manufactured assembly.
Essential for wireless signal transmission and reception, often a discrete component or integrated into the radio module.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.name: Carbon
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.reasoning: Carbon is often used as the sensing electrode material in capacitive soil moisture sensors for conductivity and capacitive sensing properties, very common but some designs use metals instead.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.name: Silicon dioxide
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.reasoning: Silicon dioxide acts as the dielectric layer in the capacitive sensor, essential for the capacitive sensing principle and widely used.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.name: Aluminum
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.reasoning: Aluminum commonly used for electrical conductors or electrodes in sensor probes due to good conductivity and corrosion resistance, but copper can be substituted.

Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.name: Epoxy resins
Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor Probe.reasoning: Epoxy resins are used as insulating and protective coatings on sensor probes, common but other resins like polyurethanes exist.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Silicon
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Silicon is the fundamental semiconductor material for microcontroller ICs, absolutely essential with no practical substitutes.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Copper
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Copper is used extensively for internal wiring and interconnects on the silicon die and package, standard industry metallization.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Gold
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Gold is used in wire bonding in microcontrollers for its excellent corrosion resistance and conductivity, but copper wire bonding is increasingly common.

Microcontroller Unit (MCU).name: Aluminum
Microcontroller Unit (MCU).reasoning: Used in some metallization layers and packaging for MCUs, common but alternatives exist.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Silicon
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Silicon is the semiconductor base for radio integrated circuits, essential for functionality.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Copper
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Copper is used for internal wiring and antenna feed lines inside the module, a standard conductor.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Aluminum
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Aluminum may be used in shielding or housing parts inside the module, but plastic housings are common alternatives.

Wireless Radio Module.name: Glass
Wireless Radio Module.reasoning: Glass can be used for packaging or as substrate parts in RF modules, but plastic substrates are also used.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Lithium
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Lithium is essential in lithium-ion or lithium polymer batteries commonly used for power supply.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Copper
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Copper is used in current collectors and wiring within batteries or energy harvesters, universally important.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Aluminum
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Aluminum is used for cathode current collector foils and packaging of batteries, a standard material.

Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.name: Graphite
Power Supply Module (Battery or Energy H.reasoning: Graphite is the primary anode material in lithium-ion batteries widely used for energy storage.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Fiberglass
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Fiberglass is the standard reinforcement material in PCB laminates (FR4), essential for mechanical strength.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Copper
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Copper is universally used for PCB copper traces and planes, essential for electrical connectivity.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Epoxy resins
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Epoxy resins are the standard polymer matrix used in PCB laminates and solder mask coatings, critical for structure and electrical isolation.

Printed Circuit Board (PCB).name: Silicon dioxide
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).reasoning: Silicon dioxide is present as filler and in glass fibers within the laminate, common but included under fiberglass composite.

Enclosure / Probe Housing.name: Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene
Enclosure / Probe Housing.reasoning: ABS is a common thermoplastic choice for sensor enclosures and probe housings providing strength and chemical resistance.

Enclosure / Probe Housing.name: Polypropylene
Enclosure / Probe Housing.reasoning: Polypropylene can also be used for housings due to chemical resistance and low cost but less rigid than ABS.

Enclosure / Probe Housing.name: Stainless steel (SS 304/316)
Enclosure / Probe Housing.reasoning: Stainless steel types 304/316 are used for durable, corrosion resistant probe housings, especially in harsh environments.

Antenna.name: Copper
Antenna.reasoning: Copper is the standard material for antenna elements due to excellent electrical conductivity and ease of fabrication.

Antenna.name: Aluminum
Antenna.reasoning: Aluminum can be used as an antenna material for lighter weight and acceptable conductivity, but less common in radio wavelength antennas.

Antenna.name: Polytetrafluoroethylene
Antenna.reasoning: PTFE is often used as a high frequency dielectric or substrate material in antenna design for its low loss properties.
